subject: chemistry

hotspots.label: Example molecules
hotspots.description: Four real molecules: O₂, H₂O, CO₂, and CH₄. Each is a team of atoms held together by covalent bonds.
hotspots.positionHint: The four ball-and-stick structures arranged in a row.
hotspots.function: Shows real molecules built from bonded atoms.

hotspots.label: The atoms in a team
hotspots.description: The spheres are the atoms. A molecule has at least two of them, from the same or different elements.
hotspots.positionHint: The individual atom spheres inside each structure.
hotspots.function: Shows the atoms that make up each molecule.

hotspots.label: Covalent bonds
hotspots.description: The highlighted joints between atoms are the covalent bonds — the shared electrons that hold each molecule together.
hotspots.positionHint: The glowing rods connecting atoms, visible when the bond-highlight layer is on.
hotspots.function: Shows the covalent bonds joining the atoms.

visualStyleNotes: Chemistry palette, Anatomy Atelier bar: warm off-white/paper background (#F7F3EC) with a soft radial vignette, no floor grid, no props. Four ball-and-stick molecules float in a row, small in frame with generous negative space, lit with soft neutral studio light — no rim-light glow, no bloom, no emissive anywhere. Clean stylized product-render look, specimen-quality not cartoon. Standard CPK ball-stick colors, desaturated: oxygen muted warm red, hydrogen warm off-white, carbon soft graphite. Strong saturated color is reserved for the small flat hotspot dots (amber / molecular-green / coral accents from the Chemistry palette). Slow auto-rotation, calm, minimal chrome.
materialNotes: Metallic-roughness PBR, metallic=0 everywhere, single 2K shared texture atlas. Oxygen spheres: muted warm red, roughness ~0.45. Hydrogen spheres: warm off-white, roughness ~0.5. Carbon spheres: soft graphite, roughness ~0.5. Bond rods: thin graphite cylinders, roughness ~0.55. No emissive channels anywhere — any glow or highlight is handled by app runtime UI.
assetBrief:
SUBJECT: four classic molecules as ball-and-stick models, built to be read as 'atoms teaming up — the smallest unit of a substance.' Three procedural layers, all clean primitives:

1) MAIN: four ball-and-stick molecules arranged in a row (spacing ~1.3): (a) O₂ — two muted-red spheres (radius ~0.34) joined by a double bond (two parallel graphite rods); (b) H₂O — one muted-red sphere (radius ~0.34) with two warm off-white spheres (radius ~0.22) at a ~104.5° bend, single rods; (c) CO₂ — one soft-graphite sphere (radius ~0.3) with two muted-red spheres in a line, double rods on each side; (d) CH₄ — one soft-graphite sphere with four warm off-white spheres in a tetrahedral arrangement, single rods. All standard CPK ball-stick geometry.

2) BOND HIGHLIGHT (toggleable layer): all bond rods brighten slightly and gain a soft rim (app-driven glow) so the joints read as covalent bonds.

3) BREAK APART (toggleable layer): the water molecule's atoms separate (app animates them drifting apart along the bond axes) leaving the O and H atoms isolated, showing a broken molecule is no longer water.

Camera: framed so all four molecules fit in a row with negative space; auto-rotate default. Budget 6-10k triangles. Named nodes: Molecule_O2, Molecule_H2O, Molecule_CO2, Molecule_CH4, Oxygens, Hydrogens, Carbons, Bonds, DetachedHydrogens. All labels are hotspot dots in the app layer.
